items.title: POI: clean up yes / no / limited values in Filters, context menu and Search
items.body:
## ToDo Clean up how values of POI additional properties (`yes` / `no` / `limited` / `only` / `designated` …) are written in `phrases.xml` and shown in **Filters**, the **POI context menu** and **Search**. Format: every value is written as `Name: value` (`Fridge: yes`, `Smoking: not allowed`, `Kayaks: yes`, `Toll: no`); `;` separates search synonyms only. The app picks the part it needs. Draft PRs: strings #26669 (English), app #26670 (filters + context menu + search, Android and OsmAnd-shared).
Context menu (now)Filters (now)
**Strings (`phrases.xml`)** — #26669 - [ ] English: 168 values inside a `poi_additional_category` → `Name: value` (`Yes;Fridge` → `Fridge: yes`, `No` → `Fridge: no`, `Allowed` → `Smoking: allowed`) - [ ] English: 169 standalone values (sentences) → `Name: value` (`No toll` → `Toll: no`, `Coins not accepted` → `Coins: no`, `Takeaway` → `Takeaway: yes`) - [ ] Rule in the header comment of `values/phrases.xml` - [ ] Translations later: convert by script (`Да;Холодильник` → `Холодильник: да`), ~7,700 strings; ~230 have no name and stay - [ ] Remove `poi_capacity_disabled_yes` (not used by any POI type) **Filters** — #26670 - [ ] Group with only one `yes` value → one **switch**, no expandable list; label = the name (**Delivery**, **Cafe**, **Drinking water refill**); with old strings the group name - [ ] All values of the group have the same name → group header + values without the name: **Changing table** → `Yes`, `Limited`, `No` - [ ] Names differ (list of options): - - [ ] name with only `yes` → the name: **Rented boats** → `Kayaks`, `Canoe` - - [ ] name with other values too → the whole string: `Adoption: yes`, `Adoption: no` - [ ] No `:` → the whole string, as now - [ ] The rules use all values of the group, not only the visible ones - [ ] Order of values stays alphabetical until there are counters **POI context menu** — #26670 - [ ] Group with one value of a property (one tag: `smoking=*`) → two lines: **Smoking** / `No` - [ ] Group of options (different tags: `boat:kayak:rental`, …) with one value → **Rented boats** / `Kayaks` - [ ] Group with several values → group title / values: `yes` → the name (`Kayaks`), other values → whole (`Kayaks: limited`), no `:` → as it is (`Cash` • `Visa`) - [ ] Standalone (non-group) values: `Name: value` → two lines **Takeaway** / `Yes` (`DefaultPoiAdditionalRowBehaviour` already splits; now with the shared parser for `:`, `：`, `︰`) - [ ] Other places that show a value as a name use the search name: `PoiUIFilter` name, `QuickSearchDialogFragment`, `SearchHistoryHelper` **Search v1 / v2** — #26670 - [ ] **Only `yes` values** of additional properties are searched (OSM value `yes`, or English `Name: yes` / old `Yes`, so `station=subway` stays). Before: everything except English "no" (v1) / keys ending in `_no` (v2) — `limited`, `designated`, `outside` were found too - [ ] **Only the part before `:`** is matched, indexed and shown: `Subway station`, not `Yes` / `Да`; old `Yes;Subway station` → first synonym, else group name — `SearchCoreFactory`, `SpatialPoiSearch`, `SpatialTextSearchAPI` - [ ] Decide: combine `only` (and `designated`?) with `yes` in one search result (`Takeaway` = takeaway yes|only) **Filter-only tags** (`takeaway_filter`, `delivery_filter`, `outdoor_seating_filter`, `shower_filter`; written into the OBF by `rendering_types.xml` tag_transform) - [ ] Now: same `Name: value` strings as the real tags (`Takeaway: yes`), no map change - [ ] Later: drop the synthetic tags and filter by the real values (yes|only) in the app; keep generating the old tags for one release for old apps - [ ] 74 charging socket tags (`osmand_socket_*`): leave as they are **Release order** - [ ] App code (#26670) before or with the new strings (#26669), otherwise the context menu shows `Fridge: Fridge: yes` - [ ] Translations after the English strings - [ ] iOS: same rules (separate task); Web: check whether it parses `phrases.xml` **Next: POI context menu redesign (proposal)** The expand arrow (Toilets has it, Delivery does not) is not fixed in the current card: the card gets a new layout. - Header in the Astronomy card style (`AstroContextMenuFragment`): name, type · distance · open status (`opening_hours`), close button, a row of round icon buttons - - [ ] Common buttons: **Directions** (primary), **Save**, **Share** - - [ ] Contextual buttons, only when the tag exists: **Call** (`phone`), **Website** (`website`), **Menu** (`website:menu`), **Wikipedia** - [ ] Below the header: Material 3 cards, one per section, each a segmented list (rows as separate segments, outer corners rounded); empty sections are hidden - [ ] Property rows have no expand arrow: tap on any property row → nearby search with this value (category filter + value), the same for grouped and standalone values. Check that `delivery:yes` is found, not only the synthetic `delivery_filter` - [ ] A section with one row is not shown as its own card: the row moves into a neighbouring section Sections (fixed order): | # | Section | Tags / groups from `poi_types.xml` | |---|---|---| | 1 | Opening hours | `opening_hours`, `service_times`, `collection_times`, `seasonal`, `operational_status`, `xmas:*` | | 2 | Contacts & address | `phone`, `website`, `contact:*`, `website:menu`, `addr:*`, `level`, `internet_access:ssid` | | 3 | Service options | `takeaway`, `delivery`, `drive_through`, `drive_in`, `reservation`, `self_service`, `self_checkout`, `home_visit`, `bulk_purchase`, `second_hand` | | 4 | Food & drinks (food and shops only) | `cuisine`, `diet`, `dish`, `cocktails`, `coffee`, `microbrewery`, `organic`, `ice_cream` | | 5 | Amenities | `toilets`, `changing_table`, `outdoor_seating`, `smoking`, `air_conditioning`, `internet_access`, `drinking_water`, `shower`, `fireplace`, `dog`, `live_music` | | 6 | Accessibility | `wheelchair`, `wheelchair:description`, `tactile_paving`, `blind:description`, `deaf:description`, `traffic_signals_sound` / `_vibration` | | 7 | Payment & prices | `payment_type`, `payment_*`, `fee`, `charge`, `price`, `membership`, `cash_withdrawal*`, `parking:fee` | | 8 | Details (title by POI type: Charging, Fuel, Piste, Climbing…) | `socket:*`, `fuel_type`, `capacity*`, `ele`, `sac_scale`, `piste_*`, `climbing:*`, `aerialway:*`, `depth`, `maxheight`… | | 9 | About | `description`, Wikipedia, photos, `start_date`, `architect`, `artist_name`, `inscription`, `name:etymology`, other names | | 10 | OSM data (collapsed, last) | OSM id, `check_date`, `note`, `ref`, Edit | Sections 3 and 5 may be merged if a typical cafe gets only 1–2 rows in each. Data: - [ ] There is no section data now: `poi_additional_category` has only `name` and `icon`; rows are sorted in one list by `order` (set on 63 of 3502 values) and then by name (`sortInfoEntries`) - [ ] Add a `section="…"` attribute in `poi_types.xml` on `poi_additional_category` and on standalone `poi_additional` (~250 groups + standalone values); shared by Android, iOS and Web. Check that nothing in the OBF depends on it - [ ] Count rows per section on real OBF data for a cafe, hotel, fuel station and charging station before fixing the list - [ ] Confirm the section list and the header buttons with design (gen by AI)

items.title: Bicycle routing: HH takes several minutes to fail before falling back to standard routing
items.body:
### Routing engine - [x] OsmAnd's in-app offline routing - [ ] Any online routing provider (YOURS, openrouteservice, OSRM, etc.) ### Routing Profile Cycling profile, Auto routing mode (HH with A* fallback). Reproduction settings: - Riding style: Prefer byways - Avoid roads: No unpaved roads enabled - Other parameters: Default ### Start and end points **Start:** Tübingen Hbf, Germany — `48.5156, 9.0556` **Destination:** Ulm Hbf, Germany — `48.3994, 9.9826` These are representative test coordinates. The original user's exact route is unavailable. With default cycling parameters, the calculated route is approximately 89.5 km. ### Actual route With the specified cycling parameters, HH routing repeatedly attempts to recalculate the route before falling back to standard A* routing. **Observed behavior:** 1. HH routing progresses to 90–99% and remains there for almost 3 minutes. 2. Logcat reports `Too many recalculations (stop)` after 30 iterations. 3. The app displays: "Fast routing is unavailable with the selected route parameters. Switching to standard calculation." 4. The progress bar drops from approximately 99% to 2% as A* begins. 5. The final route is calculated successfully, but the process takes approximately 4.5 minutes. **Measurements on the same emulator and route:** | Cycling parameters | Calculation time | |---|---| | Default | 12.3 s | | Prefer byways | 11.7 s | | No unpaved roads | 46.6 s | | Prefer byways + No unpaved roads | 264.2 s | | Same combination, repeated | 273.6 s | The reported automatic calculation restarts were not independently reproduced. The progress reset during HH → A* fallback may explain the perceived restart. ### Expected route - Avoid excessive HH recalculations when the selected routing parameters cannot be handled successfully. - Fall back to standard routing within a reasonable time instead of spending several minutes on unsuccessful HH attempts. - Clearly indicate the transition between routing algorithms without making the progress bar appear to restart unexpectedly. - Display a meaningful explanation when the selected parameters prevent fast routing. ### Maps you used (online or offline) Offline OsmAnd map: `Germany_baden-wuerttemberg_tubingen_europe_2.obf` Map edition: October 1, 2026. The World basemap was also installed. ### Your Environment OsmAnd Version: 5.4.10 (5410), Google Play Android version: Android 16 (API 36) Device model: Android Emulator (sdk_gphone64_x86_64) RAM: 4 GB CPU: 4 vCPUs Reproduction status: Partially reproduced (representative route and settings). ### Anything else? ### Reproduction Evidence — PARTIALLY REPRODUCED The issue was reproduced twice on OsmAnd 5.4.10 (Android 16 emulator) using a representative bicycle route from Tübingen to Ulm. **Test results:** - Default parameters: 12.3 seconds (HH successful). - Prefer byways + No unpaved roads: 264.2 seconds. - Repeated test: 273.6 seconds. - HH performs 30 unsuccessful recalculations before falling back to A*. - Progress reaches approximately 99%, then resets to 2% when standard routing starts. ### Video Comparison
Run 1 — HH Fallback Run 2 — Repeated Test
Error message and progress reset at ~1:17. Same behavior reproduced. Error at ~0:12.
### Screenshots
HH Routing Failure Final Route
Fast routing unavailable; switching to standard calculation. Route calculated successfully after 264 seconds.
### Conclusion **PARTIALLY REPRODUCED.** The prolonged HH recalculations, fallback to A*, and progress reset were consistently reproduced. Actual automatic route calculation restarts were not observed. The progress reset may explain the restarts reported by the user. The original user's exact route and settings were not available, so the test used a representative configuration. (gen by AI)

items.title: 'path' is silently reclassified as a 'footway'
items.body:
**(1)** We have a concerning tag conversion [here](https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd-resources/blob/13bb530595a2671f4baef431a1e0c7aa5f0b12fa/obf_creation/rendering_types.xml#L250) which I believe is factually wrong:

`	<entity_convert pattern="tag_transform" from_tag="highway" from_value="path" if_tag1="foot" if_value1="designated" if_not_region_name="$france" to_tag1="highway" to_value1="footway"/>`

This causes renderers which make the distinction between _paths_ and _footways_ (e.g. Touring view) to mis-represent affected _paths_ as _footways_ (!)

A _highway=footway_ defines the physical feature itself as a pedestrian‑specific way, while a _highway=path_ with _foot=designated_ defines the access rules, not the physical feature. In practice, 
- _footways_ often imply  smoother surfaces, better visibility, urban context, wheelchair suitability
- _paths_ often imply uneven ground, rural context, hiking difficulty (sac_scale), trail visibility issues

Hence, the distinction matters. (See also the 'strange exception' we already made for France for #17674.)

---

**(2)** Similarly, but less impactful, we also have _area paths_ become _area footways_ [here](https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd-resources/blob/13bb530595a2671f4baef431a1e0c7aa5f0b12fa/obf_creation/rendering_types.xml#L2122):

`	<entity_convert pattern="tag_transform" from_tag="area:highway" from_value="path" to_tag1="area:highway" to_value1="footway" routing="no"/>`

**(3)** Another (for now low impact) questionable conversion may be that _highway=corridor_ becomes _highway=footway_ with _tunnel=yes_ [here](https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd-resources/blob/13bb530595a2671f4baef431a1e0c7aa5f0b12fa/obf_creation/rendering_types.xml#L766):

`	<entity_convert pattern="tag_transform" from_tag="highway" from_value="corridor" to_tag1="highway" to_value1="footway" to_tag2="tunnel" to_value2="yes"/>`

 A corridor is not inherently a tunnel. This conversion loses the indoor corridor classification and invents a tunnel property. It may in principle affect rendering, routing, elevation interpretation, layer handling, and tunnel-specific warnings (but this is just a side finding, no observed issue for now).

### Actual route

as above

### Expected route

This should be the route  (car profile)
https://osmand.net/map/navigate/?start=3.080180,101.724193&end=2.997644,101.733377&profile=car#13/3.0584/101.7386

### Maps you used (online or offline)

<!-- (please tick the proper box [x]) -->
- [x ] Offline maps offered within the OsmAnd app for download. <!-- all version going back to at least 4 updates/ 2 years -->
- [ ] Online (tile / raster) maps <!-- Please name it -->


### Your Environment

```
OsmAnd Version: 5.3.10
Android version: 10
Device model: Samsung A70

```


### Anything else?

This issue pertains to motorcyle path/service roads graph weighting issue.  For this particular report, the issue is at the bypass route near the toll plaza (3.040979,101.706126). 

This also affects routing wherever there is a motorcyle path that is intended to separate riders away from the main highway. In particular these paths that parallels the following expressways in Klang valley (not sure about paths elsewhere in Malaysia)
1)  Federal Highway  [3.114829,101.675709](local name Lorong motorsikal Lebuhraya Persekutuan) all the way to the coast
2)  Guthrie Expressway [ 3.103795,101.544617] (Lebuhraya Koridor Guthrie) northwards
3)   Kesas Expressway  [3.062417,101.690016]   (Lebuhraya Shah Alam) the newer twin of Federal Highway. 

My laymen solution:  Upgrade these path/ways to have the same weighting as the highways that the cars use. These will prevent the router from suggesting weird alternative ways, or always trying to push motorcycles who are already in the path onto the highways. 

I am a delivery rider, at least 4 hours on Osmand everyday - your best tester and possibly the only one using osmand as the main map in the Asian region. Got a few more stability issues but that's for another ticket.

items.title: [FR] "PH" & "SH" translations for opening hours
items.body:
In the French version, opening hours are translated (e.g. "Mo-Fr 08:00-20:00" is translated "Lun-Ven 08:00-20:00").
So, it is also possible to translate "PH" and "SH" respectively as "Jours fériés" and "Vacances scolaires"?
For example, "Mo-Fr 08:00-20:00; PH 08:00-12:00; SH 10:00-12:00" would be translated as "Lun-Ven 08:00-20:00; Jours féries 08:00-20:00; Vacances scolaires 10:00-12:00" which is more clear than "PH" and "SH".

Thanks for updating French translation!

I'm pretty sure it is due to https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5399468686 having changed from `access=no` in `2026-06-01` base Croatia download, and incremental changes from `2026-06-26 05:10` having changed it to `access=yes` See the details of that node which lists both `No access` and `Access is allowed` **at the same time** for _"General access"_ ! items.title: R8 breaks Amenity origin IDs and POI association for Favorites and GPX waypoints
items.body:
## Description

R8 obfuscation changes the runtime class name used by `Amenity.toStringEn()`, producing unstable `amenity_origin` identifiers stored in Favorites and GPX waypoints.

Before R8, POI origins used a stable `Amenity:` prefix. In affected R8 Nightly builds, this prefix can be replaced with an obfuscated class name, such as `F6:`.

This causes two related problems:

1. **Unstable serialization:** Newly created POI Favorites and GPX waypoints store obfuscated origin identifiers instead of the historical `Amenity:` format.
2. **Cross-version compatibility:** Favorites and waypoints created in affected Nightly builds may lose their association with the original POI after updating, making some dynamically retrieved POI information unavailable.

**Related PR:** #26436

## Steps to reproduce

### 1. Verify the serialization regression

1. Install an affected R8 Nightly build.
2. Select a POI on the map, for example **City pharm (1)** in Kyiv.
3. Add the POI to Favorites.
4. Export the Favorite to an `.osf` file.
5. Inspect the `amenity_origin` field in the exported GPX.

**Broken R8:**
`F6:City pharm: healthcare:pharmacy`

**Expected stable format:**
`Amenity:City pharm: healthcare:pharmacy`

Repeat the same steps in a build containing #26436. The newly created Favorite should use the stable `Amenity:` prefix.

### 2. Verify the legacy Nightly compatibility limitation

1. In the affected R8 build, open the newly created Favorite and verify that **Type → Pharmacy** is displayed.
2. Export the Favorite to an `.osf` file.
3. Import it into a build containing the original fix from #26436.
4. Open the imported Favorite.

**Actual result:**
- The Favorite remains available.
- Its stored metadata, including opening hours, remains intact.
- However, the original POI is no longer fully resolved.
- The **Type → Pharmacy** row disappears.

The test POI has no Wikidata ID, so alternative Wikidata-based matching does not mask the origin compatibility issue.

## Expected result

- Newly created Favorites and GPX waypoints must use stable `Amenity:` origin identifiers, independent of R8 obfuscation.
- Existing pre-R8 Favorites and waypoints must retain their original identifiers without being rewritten or corrupted during upgrades, editing, importing, exporting, or synchronization.
- Previously saved user data must remain accessible.

Compatibility with origins already written by affected R8 Nightly builds is documented separately below as a known limitation.

## Root cause

Previously, `Amenity.toStringEn()` relied on the runtime Java class name to construct the origin identifier.

R8 can rename this class, causing the generated identifier to differ across builds.

For example:

**Pre-R8 / Fixed:**
`Amenity:City pharm: healthcare:pharmacy`

**Broken R8:**
`F6:City pharm: healthcare:pharmacy`

Some consumers compare these origin identifiers against values generated by the current build or expect the historical `Amenity:` prefix.

As a result, an obfuscated origin may fail to match its original POI, even though the Favorite or waypoint itself remains accessible.

Relevant components include:

- `Amenity.toStringEn()`
- `AmenitySearcher`
- `AmenityExtensionsHelper`
- `PlaceDetailsObject`
- `SelectedMapObjectsMerger`

## Fix

PR #26436 replaces the runtime class-name-based prefix with the stable `Amenity:` identifier.

This restores the historical serialization format and prevents newly created POI Favorites and GPX waypoints from receiving obfuscated origin identifiers.

The fix removes the dependency on runtime class names without introducing additional migration logic.

### Known limitation: Previously saved R8 Nightly data

Favorites and GPX waypoints created from POIs in affected R8 Nightly builds may already contain obfuscated identifiers such as `F6:`.

These identifiers are preserved after updating to the fixed version and may no longer match the original POI.

This can affect dynamically retrieved information, including the POI type, current opening status, and updated POI details.

However, further investigation confirmed:

- **Existing pre-R8 Favorites are not corrupted or rewritten.** Their `Amenity:` origins remain unchanged.
- Only Favorites and GPX waypoints **newly created from POIs** while running affected R8 Nightly builds receive obfuscated origins.
- Editing, moving, importing, exporting, and synchronizing existing Favorites do not regenerate their origin identifiers.
- Saving one new Favorite does not modify the origin identifiers of other existing Favorites.
- Affected Favorites remain accessible, including their coordinates, names, icons, and stored POI metadata.
- An affected Favorite can be repaired by recreating it from the original POI in a fixed build. Simply editing the existing Favorite does not regenerate its origin.

### Compatibility decision

We investigated adding backward-compatible origin normalization during POI lookup.

However, the obfuscated identifiers do not contain a reliable marker identifying them as historical R8-generated Amenity origins.

A generic normalization rule could interpret unrelated or future origin formats as Amenity identifiers, potentially introducing incorrect POI associations and long-term maintenance risks.

Since:

- The affected builds were Nightly-only.
- The regression was introduced with R8 on September 30, 2026.
- Previously existing Favorites and waypoints remain unchanged.
- Only POI-based points newly created during the affected Nightly period can receive the incorrect prefix.
- The saved points and their stored metadata remain accessible.

**Decision: Do not introduce heuristic read-side normalization as part of #26436.**

The PR focuses on eliminating the root cause and preserving the stable serialization format going forward.

Legacy Nightly compatibility may be reconsidered if significant user impact is reported and a sufficiently reliable identification strategy becomes available.

## Test environment

- Android 16 (API 36), x86_64 emulator
- Build variant: `androidFullOpenglX86Release`
- R8 optimization enabled
- Broken commit: `680004e15d`
- Fixed commit: `15547eee57` (original #26436 implementation)

## Evidence

### Stable serialization verification

The same POI was saved and exported in both Broken and Fixed builds.

**POI:** Kyiv

- Broken: `F6:Kyiv: administrative:city;wiki_place`
- Fixed: `Amenity:Kyiv: administrative:city;wiki_place`

The exported Favorite data was compared to confirm the expected difference in origin serialization.

### Legacy Nightly compatibility verification

**POI:** City pharm (1), Kyiv

- Broken: the newly created Favorite resolves the original POI and displays **Type → Pharmacy**.
- Fixed: after importing the same legacy Favorite, the Type row is missing.
- The original `amenity_origin` remains `F6:City pharm: healthcare:pharmacy`.
- Other stored Favorite information, including opening hours, remains available.

The reproduction uses a POI without Wikidata metadata to test origin-based matching directly.

**Reproduction file:** [[Amenity-Origin-R8-Repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33301537/Amenity-Origin-R8-Repro.zip)](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33301537/Amenity-Origin-R8-Repro.zip)

Broken/Fixed screenshots are also attached for comparison.

## Status

- **Root cause:** Identified.
- **Stable origin serialization:** Fixed in #26436.
- **Manual verification:** PASS — Broken and Fixed produce the expected different origin prefixes.
- **Existing pre-R8 data:** Confirmed to remain unchanged during normal Favorite operations.
- **Legacy R8 Nightly compatibility:** Investigated and documented as a known limitation.
- **Automatic legacy normalization:** Intentionally excluded based on the risk/benefit assessment.
- **Next step:** Final Code Review and QA verification of #26436.

The issue can be closed after the stable serialization fix passes final verification.

### Describe the idea

I find the map difficult to read, especially when it comes to labels (all labels, but especially POI labels).

Here is what I think is causing the readability issue:
- The font is too thin (zooming in on the map or increasing the text size in the settings is not a real solution).
- Character outlines are too thin
- Characters are too thin
- Depending on the zoom level and the density of POIs in an area, labels overlap other elements, making them very difficult to read

I suggest that:
- The text be bolder, or, failing that, that the character outlines be thicker.
- When a label overlaps another POI or POI label, or any object (except lines and polygons), the element that is covered should disappear.

I also suggest:
- POIs such as speed bumps and pedestrian crossings should overlap navigation lines. 
- Certain elements such as trees should be larger (almost as large as a POI).

Check above

items.title: Last checked opening hours
items.body:
### Describe the idea

It's no secret that OSM has some pretty old data at times, eg [these](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/2379058434/history#map=19/51.535281/9.935645) opening hours are 12 years old. Most aren't that extreme, but still aren't good enough to blindly trust. I always check the first party website when looking for opening hours.

### Expected behaviour

It would nice if OsmAnd could use `check_date:opening_hours` to inform users when opening hours where last checked. This tag has seen a dramatic increase in [usage](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/keys/check_date:opening_hours#overview) since StreetComplete started asking users to confirm opening hours. This could be used to add a note "These hours where last checked x weeks ago,"

There is also `opening_hours:url` which has a lot less [usage](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/keys/opening_hours:url), but if it was more popular the two could be combined to "These hours where last checked x weeks ago, for the most up to date see (link)."

### Alternatives you've considered

I have to check the first party website 100% of the time, I never know if I can trust OSM data. If I know OSM is relatively fresh, I can trust it.

### Context

Here is Googles UI. They explicitly say it was confirmed by the business, and even though OSM is getting more businesses self editing than ever before, that is a, not known, and b, not more relevant than a OSM mapper.


![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/966dc55f-0c1f-4a89-97a7-8f8267f5bfe2)

items.title: Moped routing: add "Avoid cobblestone" / "Avoid sett" parameters (as in Bicycle profile)
items.body:
### Describe the idea

The [Moped routing profile](https://osmand.net/docs/user/navigation/routing/moped-routing) has only a few route parameters (Avoid ferries, Avoid unpaved roads, Allow private access, Consider temporary limitations). Unlike the [Bicycle profile](https://osmand.net/docs/user/navigation/routing/bicycle-based-routing#route-parameters---bicycle), it has no way to avoid cobblestone / sett surfaces.

Riding a moped or scooter with small wheels on cobblestone is uncomfortable, and on wet stones it can be unsafe. In many European old towns, the fastest route often goes through such streets.

Right now the moped profile in `routing.xml` has no `surface=sett` / `surface=cobblestone` / `surface=unhewn_cobblestone` rules at all (only `smoothness` and the unpaved-related rules), so these streets count as normal paved roads.

### Expected behaviour

Add the same optional boolean parameters that the Bicycle profile already has to the Moped profile (in the "Avoid roads…" list of Route parameters on Android and iOS):

- **Avoid cobblestone** (`avoid_cobblestone`)
- **Avoid sett** (`avoid_sett`)

The Bicycle profile implementation in [routing.xml](https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd-resources/blob/master/routing/routing.xml#L1256-L1257) could be reused for the moped `<way attribute="priority">` section:

```xml
<parameter id="avoid_sett" name="Avoid sett" description="..." type="boolean" default="false"/>
<parameter id="avoid_cobblestone" name="Avoid cobblestone" description="..." type="boolean" default="false"/>
...
<if param="avoid_sett">
    <select value="0.2" t="surface" v="sett"/>
</if>
<if param="avoid_cobblestone">
    <select value="0.1" t="surface" v="cobblestone"/>
    <select value="0.05" t="surface" v="unhewn_cobblestone"/>
</if>
```

When enabled, the router should avoid streets paved with cobblestone/sett where a reasonable paved alternative exists. It may also be worth adding a mild default penalty for these surfaces in the moped profile, as the Bicycle profile does.

### Alternatives you've considered

- **Avoid unpaved roads** doesn't help: cobblestone and sett are paved surfaces.
- Avoiding specific streets manually via "Avoid roads" is slow and has to be repeated for every city.
- Using the Bicycle profile instead gives wrong speeds and access rules for mopeds.
- A custom routing.xml works, but it's not a realistic option for most users.

### Context

- Moped profile in routing.xml: https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd-resources/blob/master/routing/routing.xml#L3074-L3077
- Bicycle profile cobblestone/sett rules: https://github.com/osmandapp/OsmAnd-resources/blob/master/routing/routing.xml#L1658-L1664
- Related: #18538 (Avoid unpaved roads added to the Moped profile), #14360 (split of "No cobblestone or sett" for bicycles), #25107 (granular surface filtering)
- Docs to update after implementation: https://osmand.net/docs/user/navigation/routing/moped-routing

items.title: Prefer the street name matching the TTS language during routing
items.body:
### Describe the idea

In bilingual countries or regions (like the Region of Brussels), names can be encoded in different languages

For example:
```
name=Rue de la Loi - Wetstraat
name:fr=Rue de la Loi
name:nl=Wetstraat
```

ATM, during routing, OSMAnd is using the general `name` property and not the language specific one for TTS

Might be a good idea to use the most specific name (ie. `name:fr` if the language is set to French) and fallback on the general `name` one if nothing else exists.

The current routing experience is not that plaisant as OSMAnd reads really long street names

### Expected behaviour

Prefer the street name matching the TTS language during routing

### Alternatives you've considered

There is not workaround I can see

### Context

_No response_
